additional_info.subject: Urgent: Charging Incident at Station 170000450 – Smoke & Equipment Damage
additional_info.body:
Dear eMobility Support,
I would like to report a
serious charging incident
that occurred on
March 1, 2025
, at station
170000450
. Below are the detailed event logs:
11:17:29 (Israel Time):
Initial connection at
Connector 3
.
11:17:58 (Israel Time):
Charging started.
11:18:34 (Israel Time):
Status changed:
Connector Identity Key:
3
Status:
CHARGING → PAUSED
Pause Transaction Reason:
null → EV
Transaction Details:
Transaction ID:
87665
Connector Type:
Combo CCS - 3
Protocol:
OCPI (IL*DLK)
Transaction Reference:
04D4B681BA204...
Total Energy Delivered:
0.051 kWh
Critical Issue Reported by the Customer:
During the charging session, the customer
saw smoke coming from the charging socket
.
After the session was paused, the customer
attempted to restart charging multiple times, but the vehicle did not respond
.
When unsuccessful, they
tried to disconnect the charging cable from the vehicle but were unable to do so
.
A
technician from the vehicle importer
arrived at the scene and
disassembled the vehicle’s charging port
. According to him,
both the vehicle’s charging port and the charging cable plug had melted
.
Actions Taken:
Due to the damage, we had
to remove the cable from the charging station and replace it with a new one
.
At this stage, we
do not yet know the extent of the damage to the vehicle
, but it appears that the
charging cable plug was severely damaged
.
Request for Assistance:
We kindly request your
urgent assistance
in reviewing
all logs from the relevant time period
to determine:
Could such an incident
occur due to a charger malfunction
?
Was the damage
caused by the charger or by the vehicle
?
Do the transaction logs match the vehicle that attempted to charge until 11:40 (Israel Time)?
It is important to note that the
customer intends to file a lawsuit against us in court
.
We appreciate your
immediate support
in investigating this matter and advising on the next steps.
Looking forward to your prompt response.
Best regards,
Ziv Vinitzer

additional_info.subject: ID0410084-DC/Si-D/IL-[MP / P4 170000450] Smoke & Equipment Damage CRM:01811000705
additional_info.body:
Dear Ziv Vinitzer,
Thank you for reaching
out
to eMobility Support. My name is
Ankita
, and I will be assisting you with your following query today:
Product
: Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset
:
MP / P4 170000450
ChargerID/Serial No.
:
YB7uye
Problem Description
:  Smoke & Equipment Damage
Please find below the answers to your questions regarding the incident:
Could such an incident occur due to a charger malfunction?
After analyzing the logs, we noted the following key points:
11:17:26
– Charger was in a "pilot state A-B2."
11:17:29
– Charging session was initiated.
11:17:36
– Power delivery to the vehicle began (B2-C2 state).
11:17:56
– Precharge process started.
11:17:56
– The charger not delivering power to the EV.
11:20:08
– The session was stopped from the EV side.
11:21:27
– The plug was removed.
While the charger was not delivering power after the initial stages, we are unable to pinpoint the exact cause of this interruption at this time. To investigate this further, we have requested the ECOG logs for a more comprehensive analysis.
Was the damage caused by the charger or by the vehicle?
After the session was stopped, we identified that the charger reported a "cable temperature" error. This error likely caused subsequent unsuccessful charging attempts. At this stage, we are unable to definitively determine whether the issue originated from the vehicle or the charger. We will be able to provide further clarification once we have received the ECOG logs.
Do the transaction logs match the vehicle that attempted to charge until 11:40 (Israel Time)?
Yes,
We will provide further updates as soon as we receive the necessary ECOG logs and can analyze the situation more comprehensively.
For future reference, your case number is
0410084
, please do refer to this in all further communication regarding this issue.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Ankita Khobare

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0410084-DC/Si-D/IL-[MP / P4 170000450] Smoke & Equipment Damage CRM:01811000705
additional_info.body:
Dear Ziv Vinitzer,
We have thoroughly reviewed the logs and the situation you described. Based on our findings, it appears that the EV initially requested a low current and gradually increased the demand, but the charger was unable to deliver the expected power.
In summary, the potential causes of this issue could include:
A communication issue between the EV and charger.
A malfunction in the EV's onboard charging system or connections.
A possible loose connection or dust accumulation in the charging socket, which may have led to overheating, melting, or smoking of the plug.
To help us investigate furthe if you have any pictures of the damaged plug or socket, please feel free to share them with us  also share the EV details.
This will assist in diagnosing the problem more accurately.
If you have any further questions or concerns, do not hesitate to reach out.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Ankita Khobare

change

subject of this Email when
replying
to it.

Dear Ankita,
Thank you for your response and analysis.
The vehicle involved in the incident is a
Jeep Avenger
.
I have attached pictures of the
vehicle’s charging socket
and the

for your review.
Additionally, this morning I spoke with a
representative from the vehicle importer’s service team
.
The vehicle is currently undergoing
inspections at the workshop
.
According to the representative, a
critical power management component was damaged due to the incident
.
I assume he was referring to either the
BMS (Battery Management System) or the ECU (Electronic Control Unit)
.
We are awaiting further investigation and analysis from your side.
Please provide any additional insights regarding the findings and the possible cause of the issue.
Best regards,
